effort.activeTime: ~20-45 minutes to create the public connection and wire up OAuth; a few extra hours if you also prepare a Marketplace listing
effort.waitTime: none to let external users connect via your own OAuth link; 5-10 business days if you choose to submit a Marketplace listing

steps.title: Choose the right connection type
steps.detail: For an AI agent where outside users connect their own Notion workspaces, use a public connection (OAuth 2.0). Internal connections are scoped to a single workspace, and personal access tokens are user-scoped tokens for scripts, CLIs and tools, not an install flow for other users.

steps.title: Decide installation scope before creating anything
steps.detail: Choose 'Any workspace' (any Notion user in any workspace can install; Marketplace-eligible) or 'Selected workspaces only' (only workspaces you pick at creation; not Marketplace-eligible). Scope is set once at creation and can't be changed. For a product serving arbitrary external users, choose 'Any workspace'.

steps.title: Create the public connection in the Developer portal
steps.detail: Go to the Developer portal (https://app.notion.com/developers/connections), open the Build section of the sidebar, select Public connections, then Create new connection. Fill in the connection name and development workspace, redirect URI(s) for your OAuth callback, installation scope, and capabilities (read content, update content, insert content, etc.). Request only the capabilities your agent needs.

steps.title: Retrieve OAuth credentials
steps.detail: Open the connection's Configuration tab and copy the OAuth client ID, OAuth client secret and the Authorization URL. Store the secret in your secrets manager; never expose it client-side.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth authorization flow
steps.detail: Send users to https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and owner=user. Users pick which pages and databases to share in the page picker. Exchange the code with a POST to https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token using HTTP Basic auth (base64 of CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET) and grant_type=authorization_code. Include redirect_uri in the token request if you sent it in the authorization URL or have more than one redirect URI configured. Store the access and refresh tokens per user and workspace; refreshing (grant_type=refresh_token) returns a new access token and a new refresh token.

steps.title: Handle rate limits and errors
steps.detail: Respect HTTP 429 (rate_limited) and 529 (service_overload) and wait the Retry-After seconds. Per-connection limits are 180 requests/minute (600 on Business/Enterprise workspaces), and a separate per-workspace budget is shared by all connections. Check additional_data.rate_limit_reason; 'public_api_request_blocked' means the connection's API access is restricted and needs Notion support.

steps.title: Test with an external workspace
steps.detail: Authorize the connection from a Notion account and workspace that is not your development workspace. Confirm the page-picker step works and that your agent can only reach the shared pages.

steps.title: (Optional) List on the Notion Marketplace
steps.detail: In the Marketplace listing dashboard, go to Listings > Connections and start a new connection listing with name, description, category, tags, images, logo and the associated public connection, then submit. Notion reviews every listing (including a security review) and replies by email, typically within 5-10 business days. Only needed for discoverability; public connections work independently of Marketplace listings.

gotchas: Installation scope ('Any workspace' vs 'Selected workspaces only') is set at creation and can't be changed. Choosing 'Selected workspaces only' blocks arbitrary users and Marketplace listing, so you would need a new connection.

Users choose which pages and databases to share during OAuth, and the page picker only shows pages they have full access to. Your agent sees nothing the user didn't share, so build a 'add more pages' flow that sends them back through authorization.
Public connections act on behalf of the authorizing user. Tokens are per user and per workspace, and re-authorization may return a new access_token and refresh_token, so overwrite stored tokens.
Rate limits include a shared per-workspace budget, so you can be throttled even under your per-connection limit, and that Retry-After can exceed one minute.
The token request's redirect_uri rule is unusual: it is required if you passed redirect_uri in the authorization URL or have multiple redirect URIs configured, and otherwise not allowed.

Notion's Authorization guide has a caption saying the Authorization URL field 'populates after a public connection is submitted for review'. The Marketplace FAQ says public connections work independently of listings; if the Authorization URL is blank, build the URL yourself from the documented parameters or check the portal.

approval.process: No review gate is documented before external users can authorize an 'Any workspace' public connection; Notion's Marketplace FAQ says public connections work independently of Marketplace listings. Marketplace listing is optional and separate: Notion runs a security review and reviews every listing submission, sends feedback if changes are needed, and you can resubmit.
approval.typicalWait: none for direct OAuth use; 5-10 business days for optional Marketplace listing review
rejectionRisks: Not meeting baseline connection criteria (Marketplace listing)
Connection created with 'Selected workspaces only' scope is ineligible for Marketplace
Security review findings (required before Marketplace listing)

blockers.issue: Connection was created with 'Selected workspaces only' and outside users can't install it
blockers.whatToDo: Create a new public connection with installation scope 'Any workspace'. Scope cannot be edited.

blockers.issue: Agent can't see the user's content after OAuth
blockers.whatToDo: The user must select pages or databases in the OAuth page picker (only pages they have full access to appear). Send them back through authorization to change access.
Retrying won't help. Contact Notion support.
Read the emailed feedback, fix the brand, quality or criteria issues, and resubmit from Listings > Connections.
